_totals.note: Across both corpora the token count clears the 10M floor comfortably under any tokenizer. The floor question only gets interesting for the Telugu corpus alone, which is where the cl100k-vs-Indic gap matters.

reasoning_sft.corpus_name: Reasoning / SFT distillation mix — four sources
reasoning_sft.interpretation: English/Latin corpus - cl100k is a sensible tokenizer here and its fertility (1.563) is close to 1, so no Indic comparison is drawn. 7,607,716 tokens, below the 10M floor.

telugu_web.interpretation: The manifest's 46,173,484 cl100k tokens is a real count, but it is ~5.78x what the same text costs under an Indic tokenizer (7,991,582 MuRIL tokens). cl100k clears the 10M-token floor; MuRIL does NOT clear it. The corpus is the same size either way - the token count is a property of the tokenizer, not the data, which is exactly why fertility has to be reported, not just a token total.
